prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on your needs (how serious the injuries are, whether the other driver was uninsured, whether fault is disputed, whether you need a trial lawyer, etc.). I can help you find highly qualified options, but here’s how to choose and what to do next.

If you want a quick answer: tell me your Houston zip code or neighborhood and a bit about the crash (seriousness of injuries, if police were called, insurance issues) and I’ll pull together several well-reviewed local attorneys or firms who handle car-accident cases.

How to pick the best lawyer for your case
- Experience with car-accident cases and serious-injury law in Texas (trial experience if your case might not settle).  
- Proven results: meaningful settlements or jury verdicts in similar cases.  
- Good client reviews and a reputation among other lawyers (peers).  
- Clear contingency-fee structure (no recovery, no fee; typical contingency fee is often about one-third of recovery, but confirm).  
- Responsive communication and the time to handle your case (not overloaded).  
- Willingness to pursue litigation if the insurer won’t pay a fair amount.  
- Clean disciplinary record with the State Bar of Texas.

Practical resources to check lawyers
- Texas State Bar (lawyer search and discipline history).  
- Google/Yelp reviews and client testimonials.  
- Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, and local Bar association listings.  
- Referrals from people you trust or other attorneys (if you know any).

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases like mine (severity/type of injury)? Results?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (you or another lawyer)?  
- What’s your fee and how are costs handled?  
- What’s your strategy for my case and estimated timeline?  
- How will you keep me updated, and how quickly do you respond to calls/texts?

Red flags to watch for
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount.  
- Lack of trial experience when your case may need one.  
- Poor or evasive answers about fees and costs.  
- Unwillingness to put agreements in writing or give you references.

Immediate steps after a crash (if you’re still in the early stage)
- Get medical care and follow doctors’ instructions. Document everything.  
- Call the police and get a crash report.  
- Take photos of the scene, vehicles, injuries, and damage.  
- Get witness contact info.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurance companies without consulting a lawyer.  
- Preserve evidence (vehicle, phone video, medical records).  
- Note: Texas generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for bodily-injury claims from a car wreck (so act promptly); claims against government entities have shorter notice deadlines.

If you want, I can:
- Find several highly rated Houston personal injury attorneys who handle car wrecks (give me your zip code or neighborhood).  
- Draft a list of questions to take to consultations.  
- Explain how contingency fees and costs typically work in Texas.

Which would you like me to do next?
